Sale Prices for Homes in Baltimore, Maryland in 1978 (tibble).

Source: R/data.R
baltimore_housing_df.Rd

Data collected is on home prices and home characteristics for a particular area of Baltimore in the late 1970's. This is an identical data set to baltimore_housing except this data set contains spatial coordinates as explicit X and Y columns.

Usage

baltimore_housing_df

Format

A tibble object with an unknown projection and 211 rows and 17 columns:

  • STATION: an identification number.

  • PRICE: the price of the home (thousands of dollars).

  • NROOM: the number of rooms.

  • DWELL: unknown.

  • NBATH: the number of bathrooms.

  • PATIO: whether or not the home has a patio.

  • FIREPL: whether or not the home has a fireplace.

  • AC: whether or not the home has central air conditioning (1 = central AC, 0 = no central AC).

  • BMENT: unknown.

  • NSTOR: the number of storage spaces the home has.

  • GAR: the number of cars that can fit in the garage.

  • AGE: the age of the home (in years).

  • CITCOU: an indicator for whether the home is in the inner study area or the outer study area.

  • LOTSZ: the lot size of the home (in hundreds of square feet).

  • SQFT: the size of the home interior (in hundreds of square feet).

  • X: x-coordinate for the house with an unknown projection.

  • Y: y-coordinate for the house with an unknown projection.

Source

Data were modified from the spData R package, prepared by Luc Anselin. Originaldata were made available by Robin Durin, Case Western Research University.

References

Dubin, Robin A. (1992). Spatial autocorrelation and neighborhood quality. Regional Science and Urban Economics 22(3), 433-452.
